As long as consumers allow themselves to be milked... yes.

Exactly :P I initially left that part out, but it's disingenuous without it.

Well... yeah. The $60 price point today isn't worth the same as the $60 price point of the 1990s, but consumers aren't willing to budge on the acceptable "worth" of a AAA title, so publishers have to find other ways to monetize the IP. Namely: cut it up into DLC, such that the package that would have sold for $60 in 1990s money is now selling for closer to $120 in 2015 money. They've gotten greedy, though, with even bugfixes relegated to DLC and xpacs chopped up, not to mention microtransactions, and this will be the driving force behind the new wave of piracy.

That's a good point. One phrase I'm fond of saying is that video games are easier than ever to create, and AAA games are harder than ever to create. The amount of complexity and potential for error has grown at the same time the value they bring in has stagnated.

I think not only will we see more season passes and microtransactions, I think we are on the threshold of more old games getting dusted off for another run at your dollar. Right now, that's pretty awesome. It brought us a lot of great HD updates of older games like Age of Empires 2, Stronghold, Baldur's Gate and more.

But now imagine these two trends combined. HD updates... with season passes and DLC added. It's an executive's wet dream. Low effort, low cost, almost nothing but profit. It's coming.
